facts.label: Conflicts and perimeter distinctions
facts.text: 1. Total assets under two perimeters. The balance sheet reports "Total Assets $ 61,046,276" at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4), including securitization VIE assets at fair value. The Q2 2026 release headline says "Record Total Assets of $31.8 Billion" (Release Q2 2026 page:1) and its segment balance sheet shows a subtotal before the VIE column: "$ 31,772,112 $ 29,274,164 $ 61,046,276" (Release Q2 2026 page:7). The two are different perimeters, not an error. Effect: CP-1 and CP-2 must state whether a leverage, asset or liability figure is GAAP-consolidated or ex-VIE, and the filing's consolidated figure controls for GAAP facts. The ex-VIE basis is a management presentation. 2. Cash flow under two perimeters. The liquidity section reports cash flows on a GAAP basis and on a basis "Excluding Securitization VIEs" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:137). Same effect as above. 3. Non-GAAP earnings. Distributable earnings is defined by the company and used to compute the external manager's incentive fee (Release Q2 2026 page:4 "Distributable Earnings, a non-GAAP financial measure"). It differs from GAAP net income attributable to the registrant for the same quarter (Release Q2 2026 page:5 "Distributable Earnings (Loss) $ 185,728 $ 27,139 $ 34,177 $ 42,389 $ (137,930) $ 151,503"; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:5 "Net income attributable to Starwood Property Trust, Inc. $ 6,557 $ 129,814 $ 58,435 $ 242,069"). The notes table at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:56 "Total principal amount 4,930,750 4,330,750") predates July 2026 events that change the maturity profile: a new issue of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2029 used to redeem the 2027 Senior Notes, and repayment of the 2026 Senior Notes at maturity (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101). Effect: maturity-wall work must show the June 30, 2026 table and the July 2026 pro forma separately and label the latter as a subsequent event. 5. Secured debt totals appear in several tables with different scope: other secured financing (10-Q Q2 2026 page:49), the repayment schedule that includes securitized financing (10-Q Q2 2026 page:55) and the MD&A table with undrawn capacity (10-Q Q2 2026 page:143). facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The registrant’s financial base for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 shows a lender with higher revenue than a year earlier, rising funding cost and low GAAP earnings in the latest quarter. Revenue for the quarter was higher than a year earlier, interest expense was higher, and the credit loss line moved from a small reversal in the first quarter of 2026 to a provision in the second. Distributable earnings stayed between about 147 and 160 million dollars a quarter over the last four quarters on the company’s own definition, so the gap between GAAP and distributable earnings is the central reading issue. Debt grew over the six months while stockholders’ equity fell; the equity fall reflects dividends declared above net income. The evidence is sufficient to carry a financial base into the business, credit and evidence-trace work, with the limitations in the Gaps section: no filing after June 30, 2026, no covenant levels, an unaudited interim base, and two balance-sheet perimeters.

The FY2025 statements carry an auditor’s report dated February 25, 2026 (10-K FY2025 pages 157 and 159); the 2026 and Q3 2025 reports are unaudited. - The balance sheet consolidates securitization VIEs as separate lines: "Variable interest entity (“VIE”) assets, at fair value 30,868,147 34,493,164" and "VIE liabilities, at fair value 29,293,820 32,803,806" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4). facts.label: Evidence-based interpretation
facts.text: 1. Earnings. Net income attributable to the registrant was 6,557 in Q2 2026 against 129,814 in Q2 2025 (quarterly table). The statement shows the sources: total other income was 32,329 against 121,563 a year earlier, the credit loss provision was 30,164 against 5,666, depreciation and amortization was 35,260 against 10,371, the income tax provision was (6,224) against (671) and income attributable to non-controlling interests was (8,448) against (4,882) (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 4 and 5). The prior-year quarter included a foreign currency gain of 83,761, offset in part by a derivative loss of (101,296). Revenue rose, 513,668 against 444,283, and so did interest expense, 344,577 against 316,132. Rental income, 87,854 against 28,243, is the revenue line with the largest increase; the registrant acquired Fundamental Income Properties, LLC on July 23, 2025 (10-K FY2025 page:9), which falls between the two quarters, so the rise is consistent with that acquisition, though the filings read here do not split it out in this table. 2. Distributable earnings versus GAAP. Distributable earnings in Q2 2026 was 151,503 against 148,604 in Q3 2025, 159,545 in Q4 2025 and 147,274 in Q1 2026. The segment table shows the Commercial and Residential Lending segment at 185,728 and Corporate at (137,930). The reconciliation adds back, among other items, the credit loss provision (30,164), depreciation and amortization (35,570) and non-cash equity compensation (13,313) (Release Q2 2026 pages 4 and 5). A creditor should read cash earnings power from distributable earnings with the understanding that, per the company’s reconciliation, it removes the credit loss provision and unrealized and other non-cash items that GAAP net income includes. 3. Leverage. Total debt over stockholders’ equity rose each date from Dec 31, 2024 (2.69x) to Jun 30, 2026 (3.65x), through 3.12x at Sep 30, 2025, 3.25x at Dec 31, 2025 and 3.47x at Mar 31, 2026. In 6M 2026, debt rose by 1,599,887 (23,694,124 less 22,094,237) and stockholders’ equity fell by 296,553 (6,795,516 less 6,498,963). Unsecured notes were 20.6% of total debt at Jun 30, 2026, from 19.4% at Dec 31, 2025. 4. Payout. The company declared 0.48 a share in Q2 2026 and in Q2 2025 and 0.96 in each six-month period (10-Q Q2 2026 page:6 and page:7); distributable earnings per share was 0.40 in Q2 2026 and 0.39 in Q1 2026, below that level, and 0.78 for 6M 2026 against 0.96 declared. The accumulated deficit increased by the amount by which dividends declared exceeded net income (Calculations). Operating cash flow of 264,224 in 6M 2026 was lower than dividends paid of 356,995; over the LTM, operating cash flow of 1,090,565 was higher than dividends paid of 699,817. Operating cash flow in a lender includes loan held-for-sale flows, so the two periods are not directly comparable. 5. Cash interest. Cash paid for interest of 609,792 in 6M 2026 compares with interest expense of 673,483; the LTM cash-to-expense ratio is 92.1%. Part of the gap is non-cash amortization of deferred financing costs (about 18.4 million dollars in 6M 2026 on secured financing agreements, 10-Q Q2 2026 page:50), but the filings read here do not itemise the whole difference. 6. Interest spread. LTM interest income of 1,573,708 exceeds LTM interest expense of 1,342,180 by 231,528. The ratio is 1.17x, and it excludes servicing, rental and fair value income and the VIE net change line. 7. Funding structure and maturities. Secured and securitized financing principal is 18,932,361 of which the earliest scheduled amounts are 969,797 for the remainder of 2026 and 2,738,779 for 2027 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:55). Unsecured notes were 4,930,750 at June 30, 2026 with 900,000 due within a year then; July 2026 events removed that near-term amount (pro forma in Calculations), leaving 380,750 of convertible notes due July 15, 2027 as the first unsecured maturity. 8. Credit quality links for the next modules. Nonaccrual loans, the allowance and funding commitments sit in the credit module’s scope (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 33 and 94); this module records the allowance on loans held-for-investment (419,156) and the provision line only.

facts.label: Leverage and funding mix (carrying values, GAAP consolidated perimeter)
facts.text: Formula: total debt is secured financing agreements, net plus securitized financing, net plus unsecured senior notes, net, as printed on each balance sheet. Equity is total Starwood Property Trust, Inc. stockholders’ equity. VIE liabilities at fair value are not debt in this measure. Ratios are total debt divided by equity, rounded to two decimals. The securitized-financing exclusion is shown because the balance-sheet note states that those VIE liabilities do not have recourse to the registrant.

facts.label: Perimeter bridge: GAAP consolidated versus management ex-VIE presentation, June 30, 2026
facts.text: Inputs from the segment balance sheet (Release Q2 2026 page:7): total assets, subtotal before the securitization VIE column 31,772,112; secured financing agreements, net 14,019,547; securitized financing, net 4,811,511; unsecured senior notes, net 4,882,722. Debt on that perimeter is 23,713,780; divided by the subtotal assets the result is 74.6%. On the GAAP perimeter, total debt of 23,694,124 divided by total assets of 61,046,276 is 38.8%, and total liabilities of 53,862,850 divided by total assets is 88.2%. The two percentages answer different questions and must not be compared as a trend. The release subtotal is not simply total assets less the balance-sheet line for VIE assets (61,046,276 less 30,868,147 is 30,178,129); the difference of 1,593,983 equals the securities, intangibles and unconsolidated-entity amounts eliminated against VIE balances in the VIE column (1,540,884 plus 38,069 plus 15,030).

facts.label: Unsecured senior notes: June 30, 2026 table and July 2026 pro forma (labelled pro forma, USD thousands)
facts.text: Principal at June 30, 2026 is 4,930,750 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:56). Subsequent events (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101): 500,000 of 5.875% Senior Notes due August 15, 2029 issued to redeem the 500,000 2027 Senior Notes; 400,000 of 2026 Senior Notes repaid at maturity. Pro forma principal is 4,930,750 less 400,000 (repaid) plus 500,000 (issued) less 500,000 (redeemed), which is 4,530,750. By year: 2027 380,750 (convertible notes due July 15, 2027); 2028 500,000; 2029 1,100,000 (600,000 due April 1, 2029 plus 500,000 due August 15, 2029); 2030 1,400,000 (400,000 plus 500,000 plus 500,000); 2031 1,150,000 (550,000 plus 600,000). These add to 4,530,750. This is arithmetic on disclosed terms, not a company-reported figure.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Starwood Property Trust, Inc. is a Maryland real estate investment trust that lends against commercial and residential real estate and infrastructure, owns property through its Property Segment, and services and invests in commercial mortgage securities. It is a holding company run through wholly-owned subsidiaries and is externally managed by SPT Management, LLC, which is controlled by its chairman and chief executive and is an affiliate of Starwood Capital Group. For a creditor the central business facts are that funding is mostly secured and asset-level, that unsecured notes are issued at the registrant level and swapped to floating rates, that the July 2025 acquisition of Fundamental moved the company toward owned, long-lease net lease property, and that the manager’s fee arrangements and related-party loans make governance a monitoring topic. The most important gap is documentary: the indentures, credit agreements and the management agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) cannot be separated from willingness (what was done) and feasibility (liquidity and market access). No filing after the second quarter of 2026 is supplied, so transaction history after August 6, 2026 is unknown, not absent.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The registrant’s transaction history in the sources is a sequence of financings and one acquisition, not a single event. In the second quarter of 2026 it issued 600.0 million dollars of 6.125% Senior Notes due June 2031 on May 26, 2026 and swapped them to a floating rate of SOFR plus 2.22%, with a make-whole call before December 1, 2030 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57; page:105). In May 2026 it amended its term loan facility due September 2032, raising it by 275.0 million dollars to 971.5 million dollars and cutting the spread by 25 basis points (10-Q Q2 2026 page:105). In April 2026 it entered a one-billion-dollar revolving warehouse facility for Fundamental’s net lease acquisitions, of which 500.0 million dollars is committed and 500.0 million dollars uncommitted, with a five-year term and a rate of SOFR plus 1.55% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:50). In the first quarter of 2026 it refinanced infrastructure loans through the Starwood 2026-SIF7 CLO in January and refinanced Fundamental net lease properties through ABS FI Series 2026-1 in March with 466.4 million dollars of third party financing at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.06% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:107). The use of proceeds is stated for the May 2026 notes: the 10-Q says the 2026 Senior Notes were repaid with proceeds of the issuance in the second quarter (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57). Status of these items is completed as of June 30, 2026.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Manager economics and control. Evidence: the base fee is a percentage of defined stockholders’ equity, the incentive fee needs core earnings above a hurdle, and removal triggers a fee of three times the average annual fees (10-K FY2025 pages 26, 237 and 238). Risk mechanic: the base fee does not fall with asset quality or leverage, and the cost of removal reduces the board’s practical ability to change manager if performance weakens. Credit implication: manager alignment with creditors rests on board oversight rather than on contract terms the creditor can observe; monitoring posture should track fees against earnings, and the credit module should record that the management agreement itself is not supplied. Counter-evidence: no incentive fee was incurred in the second quarter of 2026, and half of any incentive fee is paid in shares. 2. Related-party lending. Evidence: ten board-approved related-party loan transactions, including loans where the registrant lacks certain co-lender consent rights because of an affiliate’s interest (10-Q Q2 2026 page:69). Risk mechanic: a lender to affiliate-connected borrowers may have weaker control in a workout and faces a conflict between the manager’s affiliates and the registrant. Credit implication: concentration to affiliate-connected borrowers is an open monitoring item; the sources give transaction-level amounts but no aggregate, so no exposure conclusion is drawn. 3. Funding access and maturity management. Evidence: regular unsecured, term loan, CLO and ABS financings in 2025 and 2026, with the July 2026 notes replacing the 2026 and January 2027 maturities (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101). Risk mechanic: refinancing earlier than maturity extends the maturity profile and reduces reliance on a single market, but the registrant’s funding is mostly secured on pledged assets, and access depends on collateral values. Credit implication: refinancing risk in the near term is reduced for unsecured debt; the credit module should test secured maturities, availability and covenant headroom. Counter-evidence: leverage in the financial base rose over the same period. 4. Shift toward owned net lease property. Evidence: Fundamental’s 100.0% occupancy and 16.8 year weighted remaining lease term (10-Q Q2 2026 page:141) and ABS debt service coverage covenants (10-Q Q2 2026 page:52). Risk mechanic: long contracted rents add revenue visibility, while ABS debt at special purpose vehicles is secured on those properties and is structurally ahead of unsecured claims on them; covenants at the vehicle can restrict cash release. Credit implication: property income is more predictable, but cash reaching the registrant depends on vehicle-level tests whose levels are not supplied. 5. Key uncertainty. Management’s statement that it expects to resolve nearly 900 million dollars of underperforming assets is Management Language (Release Q2 2026 page:1); the nonaccrual loan evidence belongs to the credit module (10-Q Q2 2026 page:33).

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with bounded limitations, so the overall view is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and no consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. The evidence is a full annual report for FY2025, three quarterly reports (Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026) and three earnings releases that carry segment statements and a distributable-earnings reconciliation. The strongest contrary evidence is what is absent: no executed indenture, credit agreement or management agreement, no rating or quote input, no investor presentation, and no report for any period after June 30, 2026 although the as-of date is 2026-11-05. 1. Total assets under two perimeters. The balance sheet reports "Total Assets $ 61,046,276" at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4), including securitization VIE assets at fair value. The Q2 2026 release headline says "Record Total Assets of $31.8 Billion" (Release Q2 2026 page:1) and its segment balance sheet shows a subtotal before the VIE column: "$ 31,772,112 $ 29,274,164 $ 61,046,276" (Release Q2 2026 page:7). The two are different perimeters, not an error. Effect: CP-1 and CP-2 must state whether a leverage, asset or liability figure is GAAP-consolidated or ex-VIE, and the filing's consolidated figure controls for GAAP facts. The ex-VIE basis is a management presentation.
2. Cash flow under two perimeters. The liquidity section reports cash flows on a GAAP basis and on a basis "Excluding Securitization VIEs" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:137). Same effect as above.

3. Non-GAAP earnings. Distributable earnings is defined by the company and used to compute the external manager's incentive fee (Release Q2 2026 page:4 "Distributable Earnings, a non-GAAP financial measure"). It differs from GAAP net income attributable to the registrant for the same quarter (Release Q2 2026 page:5 "Distributable Earnings (Loss) $ 185,728 $ 27,139 $ 34,177 $ 42,389 $ (137,930) $ 151,503"; 10-Q Q2 2026 page:5 "Net income attributable to Starwood Property Trust, Inc. $ 6,557 $ 129,814 $ 58,435 $ 242,069"). A release figure cannot silently replace a filed GAAP figure.

4. Debt after the balance-sheet date. The notes table at June 30, 2026 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:56 "Total principal amount 4,930,750 4,330,750") predates July 2026 events that change the maturity profile: a new issue of 5.875% Senior Notes due 2029 used to redeem the 2027 Senior Notes, and repayment of the 2026 Senior Notes at maturity (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101). Effect: maturity-wall work must show the June 30, 2026 table and the July 2026 pro forma separately and label the latter as a subsequent event.

5. Secured debt totals appear in several tables with different scope: other secured financing (10-Q Q2 2026 page:49), the repayment schedule that includes securitized financing (10-Q Q2 2026 page:55) and the MD&A table with undrawn capacity (10-Q Q2 2026 page:143). They are not reconciled here. Downstream modules must tie them before use.
### Coverage accounting

Retained for downstream use: financial statements and notes, segment data, debt and liquidity tables, covenant and compliance statements, cash flow, subsequent-event notes, market-risk item, legal proceedings ("no material legal proceedings are pending", 10-Q Q2 2026 page:154) and exhibit lists for all periodic reports. Explicit gaps: items listed under Gaps. Evidenced exclusions: none; no content was excluded. Unknown values are not treated as zero anywhere in this answer.
## Calculations

No new calculation was made. CP-0 does not normalise, reconcile or calculate figures. The only arithmetic is the coverage count: 4 periodic reports plus 3 releases is 7 issuer sources; chunk counts 284, 155, 138, 156, 10, 6 and 7 sum to 756. The count of seven shown in the sources table was checked against the run's printed source list.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

The financial base is usable for the credit view, with the perimeter stated on every figure. | Medium | Distributable earnings is a company measure and the consolidated balance sheet includes large securitization VIE balances. |

### Financial base view

The registrant’s financial base for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 shows a lender with higher revenue than a year earlier, rising funding cost and low GAAP earnings in the latest quarter. Revenue for the quarter was higher than a year earlier, interest expense was higher, and the credit loss line moved from a small reversal in the first quarter of 2026 to a provision in the second. Distributable earnings stayed between about 147 and 160 million dollars a quarter over the last four quarters on the company’s own definition, so the gap between GAAP and distributable earnings is the central reading issue. Debt grew over the six months while stockholders’ equity fell; the equity fall reflects dividends declared above net income. The evidence is sufficient to carry a financial base into the business, credit and evidence-trace work, with the limitations in the Gaps section: no filing after June 30, 2026, no covenant levels, an unaudited interim base, and two balance-sheet perimeters.
### Source and perimeter context

- Statements are the consolidated statements of Starwood Property Trust, Inc. and subsidiaries, in USD thousands (10-Q Q2 2026 page:3 "Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets (Unaudited, amounts in thousands, except share data)"; 10-K FY2025 page:159 "Consolidated Balance Sheets (Amounts in thousands, except share data)"). The FY2025 statements carry an auditor’s report dated February 25, 2026 (10-K FY2025 pages 157 and 159); the 2026 and Q3 2025 reports are unaudited.

- The balance sheet consolidates securitization VIEs as separate lines: "Variable interest entity (“VIE”) assets, at fair value 30,868,147 34,493,164" and "VIE liabilities, at fair value 29,293,820 32,803,806" (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4). The balance-sheet note states that securitized financing issued by VIEs "do not have recourse to Starwood Property Trust, Inc." (10-Q Q2 2026 page:4).

- The release segment statements show a subtotal before a "Securitization VIEs" column; the Q2 2026 release headline total assets figure is that subtotal (Release Q2 2026 page:1 "Record Total Assets of $31.8 Billion"; page:7). The perimeter bridge in the Calculations section ties the two.

- Quarter, six-month, nine-month, full-year and LTM labels are kept distinct throughout. Q4 2025 comes from the year-end release (Release YE2025 pages 5 and 6) and ties to FY2025 less nine months 2025 (see Calculations).

- The registrant is externally managed (10-Q Q2 2026 page:11); management fees are a separate expense line and the company’s distributable earnings measure is used to compute the incentive fee (Release Q2 2026 page:4).

2. Distributable earnings versus GAAP. Distributable earnings in Q2 2026 was 151,503 against 148,604 in Q3 2025, 159,545 in Q4 2025 and 147,274 in Q1 2026. The segment table shows the Commercial and Residential Lending segment at 185,728 and Corporate at (137,930). The reconciliation adds back, among other items, the credit loss provision (30,164), depreciation and amortization (35,570) and non-cash equity compensation (13,313) (Release Q2 2026 pages 4 and 5). A creditor should read cash earnings power from distributable earnings with the understanding that, per the company’s reconciliation, it removes the credit loss provision and unrealized and other non-cash items that GAAP net income includes.

3. Leverage. Total debt over stockholders’ equity rose each date from Dec 31, 2024 (2.69x) to Jun 30, 2026 (3.65x), through 3.12x at Sep 30, 2025, 3.25x at Dec 31, 2025 and 3.47x at Mar 31, 2026. In 6M 2026, debt rose by 1,599,887 (23,694,124 less 22,094,237) and stockholders’ equity fell by 296,553 (6,795,516 less 6,498,963). Unsecured notes were 20.6% of total debt at Jun 30, 2026, from 19.4% at Dec 31, 2025.

4. Payout. The company declared 0.48 a share in Q2 2026 and in Q2 2025 and 0.96 in each six-month period (10-Q Q2 2026 page:6 and page:7); distributable earnings per share was 0.40 in Q2 2026 and 0.39 in Q1 2026, below that level, and 0.78 for 6M 2026 against 0.96 declared. The accumulated deficit increased by the amount by which dividends declared exceeded net income (Calculations). Operating cash flow of 264,224 in 6M 2026 was lower than dividends paid of 356,995; over the LTM, operating cash flow of 1,090,565 was higher than dividends paid of 699,817. Operating cash flow in a lender includes loan held-for-sale flows, so the two periods are not directly comparable.

5. Cash interest. Cash paid for interest of 609,792 in 6M 2026 compares with interest expense of 673,483; the LTM cash-to-expense ratio is 92.1%. Part of the gap is non-cash amortization of deferred financing costs (about 18.4 million dollars in 6M 2026 on secured financing agreements, 10-Q Q2 2026 page:50), but the filings read here do not itemise the whole difference.

6. Interest spread. LTM interest income of 1,573,708 exceeds LTM interest expense of 1,342,180 by 231,528. The ratio is 1.17x, and it excludes servicing, rental and fair value income and the VIE net change line.

7. Funding structure and maturities. Secured and securitized financing principal is 18,932,361 of which the earliest scheduled amounts are 969,797 for the remainder of 2026 and 2,738,779 for 2027 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:55). Unsecured notes were 4,930,750 at June 30, 2026 with 900,000 due within a year then; July 2026 events removed that near-term amount (pro forma in Calculations), leaving 380,750 of convertible notes due July 15, 2027 as the first unsecured maturity.

8. Credit quality links for the next modules. Nonaccrual loans, the allowance and funding commitments sit in the credit module’s scope (10-Q Q2 2026 pages 33 and 94); this module records the allowance on loans held-for-investment (419,156) and the provision line only.

### Business and transaction view

Starwood Property Trust, Inc. is a Maryland real estate investment trust that lends against commercial and residential real estate and infrastructure, owns property through its Property Segment, and services and invests in commercial mortgage securities. It is a holding company run through wholly-owned subsidiaries and is externally managed by SPT Management, LLC, which is controlled by its chairman and chief executive and is an affiliate of Starwood Capital Group. For a creditor the central business facts are that funding is mostly secured and asset-level, that unsecured notes are issued at the registrant level and swapped to floating rates, that the July 2025 acquisition of Fundamental moved the company toward owned, long-lease net lease property, and that the manager’s fee arrangements and related-party loans make governance a monitoring topic. The most important gap is documentary: the indentures, credit agreements and the management agreement are not supplied, so legal capacity (what the documents permit) cannot be separated from willingness (what was done) and feasibility (liquidity and market access). No filing after the second quarter of 2026 is supplied, so transaction history after August 6, 2026 is unknown, not absent.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The registrant’s transaction history in the sources is a sequence of financings and one acquisition, not a single event. In the second quarter of 2026 it issued 600.0 million dollars of 6.125% Senior Notes due June 2031 on May 26, 2026 and swapped them to a floating rate of SOFR plus 2.22%, with a make-whole call before December 1, 2030 (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57; page:105). In May 2026 it amended its term loan facility due September 2032, raising it by 275.0 million dollars to 971.5 million dollars and cutting the spread by 25 basis points (10-Q Q2 2026 page:105). In April 2026 it entered a one-billion-dollar revolving warehouse facility for Fundamental’s net lease acquisitions, of which 500.0 million dollars is committed and 500.0 million dollars uncommitted, with a five-year term and a rate of SOFR plus 1.55% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:50). In the first quarter of 2026 it refinanced infrastructure loans through the Starwood 2026-SIF7 CLO in January and refinanced Fundamental net lease properties through ABS FI Series 2026-1 in March with 466.4 million dollars of third party financing at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.06% (10-Q Q2 2026 page:107). The use of proceeds is stated for the May 2026 notes: the 10-Q says the 2026 Senior Notes were repaid with proceeds of the issuance in the second quarter (10-Q Q2 2026 page:57). Status of these items is completed as of June 30, 2026.

Subsequent events after June 30, 2026, as stated in the Q2 2026 quarterly report (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101): in July 2026 the registrant issued 500.0 million dollars of 5.875% Senior Notes due August 15, 2029 and used the proceeds to redeem the 500.0 million dollars of 2027 Senior Notes due January 15, 2027, recognising a derivative loss of 6.3 million dollars on the hedge unwind; it repaid the 400.0 million dollars of 2026 Senior Notes at maturity; it refinanced Fundamental net lease properties through ABS FI Series 2026-2 with 321.0 million dollars of third party financing at a weighted average fixed rate of 5.47%; it redeemed at par the third party financing of the STWD 2021-FL2 and STWD 2022-FL3 CLOs and amended a commercial credit facility, increasing its maximum size by 1.2 billion dollars to 3.0 billion dollars. These are subsequent events and are not folded into the June 30, 2026 balance sheet or the maturity table; the financial base handoff shows the unsecured-note pro forma separately.

In 2025 the principal transaction was the acquisition of Fundamental Income Properties, LLC by merger on July 23, 2025 for about 2.2 billion dollars inclusive of 1.3 billion dollars of assumed indebtedness; the merger was treated as an asset acquisition, with debt assumed of 878.3 million dollars of ABS financing and 400.6 million dollars of revolving secured financing (10-K FY2025 page:9; page:188). 2. Description of the January 2026 infrastructure securitization. 3. Corporate debt transactions in the second quarter of 2026. The release says, at Release Q2 2026 page:1, "our $2.1 billion of corporate debt transactions in the quarter". The filings itemise 600.0 million dollars of notes and a 275.0 million dollar term loan upsize among other items; the full composition of the 2.1 billion dollar aggregate is not itemised in the pages read. ### Credit translations

1. Manager economics and control. Evidence: the base fee is a percentage of defined stockholders’ equity, the incentive fee needs core earnings above a hurdle, and removal triggers a fee of three times the average annual fees (10-K FY2025 pages 26, 237 and 238). Risk mechanic: the base fee does not fall with asset quality or leverage, and the cost of removal reduces the board’s practical ability to change manager if performance weakens. Credit implication: manager alignment with creditors rests on board oversight rather than on contract terms the creditor can observe; monitoring posture should track fees against earnings, and the credit module should record that the management agreement itself is not supplied. Counter-evidence: no incentive fee was incurred in the second quarter of 2026, and half of any incentive fee is paid in shares.

2. Related-party lending. Evidence: ten board-approved related-party loan transactions, including loans where the registrant lacks certain co-lender consent rights because of an affiliate’s interest (10-Q Q2 2026 page:69). Risk mechanic: a lender to affiliate-connected borrowers may have weaker control in a workout and faces a conflict between the manager’s affiliates and the registrant. Credit implication: concentration to affiliate-connected borrowers is an open monitoring item; the sources give transaction-level amounts but no aggregate, so no exposure conclusion is drawn.

3. Funding access and maturity management. Evidence: regular unsecured, term loan, CLO and ABS financings in 2025 and 2026, with the July 2026 notes replacing the 2026 and January 2027 maturities (10-Q Q2 2026 page:101). Risk mechanic: refinancing earlier than maturity extends the maturity profile and reduces reliance on a single market, but the registrant’s funding is mostly secured on pledged assets, and access depends on collateral values. Credit implication: refinancing risk in the near term is reduced for unsecured debt; the credit module should test secured maturities, availability and covenant headroom. Counter-evidence: leverage in the financial base rose over the same period.

4. Shift toward owned net lease property. Evidence: Fundamental’s 100.0% occupancy and 16.8 year weighted remaining lease term (10-Q Q2 2026 page:141) and ABS debt service coverage covenants (10-Q Q2 2026 page:52). Risk mechanic: long contracted rents add revenue visibility, while ABS debt at special purpose vehicles is secured on those properties and is structurally ahead of unsecured claims on them; covenants at the vehicle can restrict cash release. Credit implication: property income is more predictable, but cash reaching the registrant depends on vehicle-level tests whose levels are not supplied.

5. Key uncertainty. Management’s statement that it expects to resolve nearly 900 million dollars of underperforming assets is Management Language (Release Q2 2026 page:1); the nonaccrual loan evidence belongs to the credit module (10-Q Q2 2026 page:33).

4. Repurchase capacity: authorisation of 400.0 million dollars less 29.9 million dollars repurchased in the first half of 2026 equals 370.1 million dollars, which matches the stated remaining capacity.

### Credit view

Starwood Property Trust, Inc. is an adequately funded real estate lender whose credit quality is weakening at the margin. Its strongest support is funding access: it issued USD 600.0 million of unsecured notes in May 2026 and USD 500.0 million in July 2026, cleared its 2026 and January 2027 maturities, and has USD 1,399.0 million of lender-approved undrawn secured capacity. Its weakest point is earnings against leverage: second quarter 2026 net income attributable was USD 6.6 million, distributable earnings per share trailed the dividend, and debt to stockholders’ equity rose to 3.65x from 3.25x, with nonaccrual loans near USD 947.3 million. Resolution of those loans and continued secured funding decide the outcome.
### Key findings

First, the registrant’s financial risk has risen over the first half of 2026. Total debt on the balance sheet increased to USD 23,694.1 million from USD 22,094.2 million while stockholders’ equity fell to USD 6,499.0 million from USD 6,795.5 million, because dividends declared of USD 357.3 million exceeded net income attributable of USD 58.4 million (Analyst Interpretation on the cause; the amounts are Documentary Fact). The mechanic is simple: a payout above earnings is paid from cash that is then replaced with debt or retained-earnings erosion, so the equity layer that sits beneath every creditor shrinks.

Second, earnings are weak on the filed basis and only adequate on the company basis. The registrant reported net income attributable of USD 6.6 million for the second quarter of 2026 against distributable earnings of USD 151.5 million, a company measure that removes the credit loss provision and unrealized items. Distributable earnings per share of USD 0.78 for the first half trailed dividends declared of USD 0.96 per share, a ratio of 0.81x. The credit implication is that the dividend is not covered by either measure, so the registrant depends on asset resolution and deployment of capital to close the gap (Documentary Fact for the figures; Analyst Interpretation for the reading).

Third, asset quality is the swing factor. The registrant had about USD 947.3 million of loans on nonaccrual at June 30, 2026 by our sum of the amounts the quarterly report states, 36.8% of commercial loans at amortized cost carry loan-to-stabilized-value above 70%, and that bucket holds USD 362.0 million of the USD 406.2 million commercial credit loss allowance. Interest stops accruing on nonaccrual loans, which lowers net interest income and ties up capital that supports the leverage ratio; foreclosures in the first half added USD 347.5 million of owned property. Management says it expects to resolve nearly USD 900 million of underperforming assets by year end or shortly after, which is Management Language and not evidence of resolution.

Fourth, funding structure is a strength with a catch. Most debt is matched-term secured funding, 68% of repurchase agreements do not permit valuation adjustments based on capital market events, and the registrant refinanced USD 1,100.0 million of unsecured notes in the quarter and the month after. The catch is rank and opacity: USD 18,932.4 million of secured and securitized financing is secured on pledged assets, corporate term loans of USD 2,533.1 million are secured on subsidiary equity, and the USD 4,930.8 million of unsecured notes rank behind both on those assets. Covenant levels are not supplied, so headroom is Not calculable even though the registrant states compliance.

Fifth, governance adds a monitoring item. The registrant is externally managed by an affiliate of its sponsor, the management agreement was not negotiated at arm’s length and carries a termination fee of three times average annual fees, and several loans were made to borrowers connected to affiliates of the manager with board approval. The mechanic is weaker creditor control rather than an observed loss; no creditor-adverse action was found in the pages read (Insufficient Information on the documents).
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The registrant has proven access to secured and unsecured markets (Documentary Fact): 2025 saw a USD 534.4 million share issuance, USD 1,550.0 million of new senior notes and a USD 700.0 million term loan, and 2026 added a USD 600.0 million note, a USD 275.0 million term loan upsizing and several securitizations, which reduces refinancing risk. The funding is mostly matched to assets, with the next four quarters of projected principal inflows exceeding projected required financing repayments by USD 785.1 million (Documentary Fact, company projection), so asset repayments fund most secured maturities. The platform is diversified across commercial lending, infrastructure lending, owned property and servicing, with a named special servicing portfolio of USD 93.6 billion (Documentary Fact), which gives several earnings sources. The unsecured note stack is long-dated after July 2026: the first unsecured maturity is the USD 380.8 million convertible notes in July 2027 (Analyst Interpretation from the maturity table). About 79% of unsecured principal is swapped to floating rates, which matches floating-rate assets but adds hedge counterparty exposure (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. Leverage has risen at each balance sheet date in the financial base, to 3.65x total debt to stockholders’ equity (Documentary Fact for the inputs, calculated ratio). Earnings do not cover the dividend, and GAAP interest cover is 1.22x on a trailing basis (Analyst Interpretation, includes fair value and consolidated VIE items). Nonaccrual loans of about USD 947.3 million and an office share of 17.6% of the commercial portfolio concentrate asset-quality risk (Documentary Fact; sum calculated). The structure is complex: GAAP assets include USD 30,868.1 million of securitization VIE assets, and the registrant states it is not obligated to provide financial support to those VIEs, so ratios on different perimeters are not comparable (Documentary Fact). Governance is the sponsor’s: manager fees, a termination fee and related-party loans reduce creditor control (Documentary Fact; creditor effect is Analyst Interpretation). The most important evidence is missing: governing debt documents, covenant levels, guarantor terms and ratings are not supplied (Insufficient Information), and no filing covers the period after the second quarter of 2026.

9. Floating share of unsecured notes: swapped notional 3,875,000 divided by principal 4,930,750 is 78.6%.
10. Secured and unsecured mix: unsecured 4,930,750 divided by (secured and securitized 18,932,361 plus unsecured 4,930,750) is 20.7% of principal.
11. Corporate-level debt: unsecured notes 4,930,750 plus term loans and revolver outstanding 2,533,102 is 7,463,852.
12. Unsecured notes issued in the second quarter and July 2026: 600,000 plus 500,000 is 1,100,000, refinancing 400,000 plus 500,000 of maturities.
